repo_notes.content: SCOPE — what this repository is and is not. The product is OSLogLoggingMiddleware, a request/response logging middleware for clients and servers generated by Apple swift-openapi-generator, backed by os.Logger. It descends from Apple's logging-middleware-oslog-example in the swift-openapi-generator repo and keeps that example's shape (a BodyLoggingPolicy enum, process() splitting each body into a half to log and a half to hand on). It is not a transport, not a client, and not cross-platform: the whole module sits inside #if canImport(Darwin) and compiles to an empty module elsewhere. Several root-level files are process artefacts, not product documentation: CLAUDE.md is agent instructions, REVIEW.md steers automated PR review, and .spi.yml points Swift Package Index at the DocC target.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, in precedence order. The DocC catalogue at Sources/OSLogLoggingMiddleware/OSLogLoggingMiddleware.docc/ is authoritative for architecture and direction; where it and readme.md disagree the catalogue wins. Design.md holds every load-bearing decision with the alternative that was rejected — transport-free dependency set, the Darwin guard, the privacy defaults, the os.Logger platform floor, the semver contract. TechDebt.md is the numbered TD-n register (each entry with Cost and Discharge); Roadmap.md is planned work in priority order. readme.md is consumer-facing install/usage and defers to the catalogue.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: CONSUMER CONSTRAINTS that any useful page set must convey. The package requires Apple platforms only (macOS 11 / iOS 14 / tvOS 14 / watchOS 7 / visionOS 1 — os.Logger's availability) and depends on OpenAPIRuntime + HTTPTypes only; the consumer brings the transport (URLSession, AsyncHTTPClient, Hummingbird…), which is also what makes the same type usable as ServerMiddleware. Privacy defaults are load-bearing: bodies are never logged unless opted in (bodyLoggingConfiguration: .never), logged bodies interpolate at .auto privacy unless publicBodies is set, and lines emit at .debug which is not persisted on device — a default flip is a major version. Semver is a contract: dependency/manifest-only changes are patches, additive API is minor. Known debts: the default Logger subsystem is still Apple's example namespace com.apple.swift-openapi (TD-1, discharge deferred to 2.0 because existing log filters would break), and no test observes the emitted line (TD-2), and nothing in this repository's own CI can catch an undeclared-but-transitively-available import (TD-3).
